pages.heading: CONSIDER YOUR ORIGINS
pages.text:
You were not made to live as brutes, but to follow virtue and knowledge.
— Dante Alighieri, Inferno

pages.heading: MESSINA · THE FIFTEENTH CENTURY
pages.text: In a Sicily darkened by famine and plague, the roads fill with those who have lost their homes. Among them walks one whom the faithful call Hollow.

pages.heading: A SHELTER ABOVE SUFFERING
pages.text: Beyond the forest stands Babel. Its builders once believed that stone could lift them beyond disaster. Their first letters praised Nero as a savior.

pages.heading: WHEN FAITH BECAME A THRONE
pages.text: But the tower was never high enough. Nero's prayers hardened into commands. He demanded longer toil, deeper obedience—and finally the worship that heaven had denied him.

pages.heading: THE VOICE ABOVE THE BELLS
pages.text: Princess Livia entered the tower with a promise of refuge for her people. Nero made her his captive: a living pledge that nobody would abandon his heaven.

pages.heading: THE HOLLOW PILGRIM
pages.text: You came seeking shelter, not a crown. Yet beyond the ruined gate, a woman's voice survives the bells. To leave her here would be to become another stone in Nero's tower.

pages.heading: ENTER BABEL
pages.text: At the threshold, an old warning asks you to abandon hope. Carry it inside instead. Find a blade. Follow the voices. Bring Livia back to the world below.
